name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: a seasonal re-mark of the auto block, a wider discount, and a HOLD
frontmatter.summary: The red-team revision re-marks the automotive block on a seasonally adjusted FY2026 income rather than the annualised Q3 peak, values the directly held toll concession rights and widens the discount to the peer midpoint. The October print is demand-positive but net destocking, and Astra's own Daihatsu retail trails the market. The sum of the parts still gives back roughly today's price after the cost-of-equity roll. HOLD, -0.7% expected return to Rp4,567.
thesis: The parts are worth Rp4,276 per share after a 35% discount taken from the method card's range, not from the share price; the base sum of the parts sits below the Rp5,000 price, so the return before the roll is negative [S0, S15, S21, S22, S23, S27].

The automotive block, the largest part, is now marked on a seasonally adjusted FY2026 income: the company's own FY2025 quarters show the fourth quarter at about two-thirds of the third, and we apply that ratio rather than annualising the Q3 peak [S14, S5, S4, F3, F32, F147].

The unlisted blocks now sit on floors we can source: infrastructure at the book of its own equity stakes plus the directly held toll concession rights, property on the listed subsidiary's market value applied to the group's asset base, and financing on a normalised return the credit trend supports [S15, S27, S26].

The discount sits at the midpoint between Astra's own peer level and the peer median; the published bear carries the peer median and the bull the name's own level, and the HOLD survives the whole thirty-to-forty per cent band [S0, S15].

The tails are discount-path probabilities, disclosed as narrower than a true operating set; the operating breaks the engine cannot reprice, including the mining non-recovery that is eighteen per cent of gross value, are quantified in the text and said to understate the published bear [S15, S14, S26].

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and ongoing with no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14].

blocks.text: **What changed.** This revision answers the red team and moves the rating from ADD to HOLD on three corrections rather than on the October print. First, the automotive block is re-marked on a seasonally adjusted FY2026 income: the company's own FY2025 quarters put the fourth quarter at about two-thirds of the third, so annualising the Q3 peak overstated the largest block by about a fifth [S14, S5, S4, F3, F32, F147]. Second, the discount moves up to 35%, between Astra's own level in the house peer set and the peer median, and the directly held toll concession rights are added at book [S15, F146, cov_publish comps]. Third, the October GAIKINDO print is demand-positive but net destocking: wholesale 81,482 and retail 82,429, with retail 947 units above wholesale in the month [S20, F101, F102, F139, F143]. The target falls to Rp4,567 and the rating is HOLD.

**The call.** Target Rp4,567 against Rp5,000, an expected total return of -0.7% including Rp399 of dividends: **HOLD**. The base path is Rp4,584; the bear Rp4,270 at 30% and the bull Rp4,894 at 25%. The return is not a discount recovery: the base sum of the parts of Rp4,276 sits below the Rp5,000 price, so the un-rolled return — the parts plus the Rp399 dividend against the price — is negative, and only the 14.6% one-year roll takes it to -0.7%. That is inside the HOLD band and well below the ten per cent ADD threshold, so the call no longer depends on the roll clearing a line [S0, S15].

**Variant view.** The market capitalises the parts at roughly the discount we now hold. Our base is 35%: the peer median is just under two fifths, Astra''s own level in the house peer set is thirty per cent, and we take the midpoint because the risk facts — no dated narrowing catalyst and related-party purchases near a quarter of revenue — argue wider than thirty per cent but do not warrant importing a small-cap median into a blue-chip [S0, S6, F21, cov_publish comps]. The published bear carries the peer median and the bull Astra''s own level; Section four shows the base target across the card range, and the HOLD survives the whole thirty-to-forty per cent band (it turns ADD only at the range floor). No dated catalyst exists, so we do not underwrite a narrowing [S8, S14, S16].

**Bias audit, signed.** The stack is no longer optimistic on the largest block: the auto mark is on a seasonal FY2026 income, not the Q3 peak. It is optimistic, not conservative, in the discount: the 35% base sits below the peer median of just under two fifths, and a smaller discount produces a higher target, so against that median the choice is the more optimistic one on value; it is conservative only against Astra's own thirty per cent level in the house set, and the discount sensitivity from the floor to two fifths in the valuation section shows the HOLD survives the band either way [cov_publish comps]. It is also optimistic in four smaller places: the financing return at the annualised actual rather than a haircut; the infra and property floors, which rise with the toll concession rights; the buyback at the completed pace; and the cost ratio declining only as revenue outgrows inflation, which is arithmetic rather than a cost-cut forecast. It is conservative in one: capex is at the audited IDR18.46tn rather than the lower data-pack figure. One disclosure is neither: the published bear holds the listed stakes at market and therefore understates the operating downside by roughly three hundred rupiah per share, which we say in the risk section rather than leave in the table [S15, F108]. Net: the call is a HOLD with essentially no margin either way — the base is flat against the price after the roll — and we do not present it as a balanced or a cheap entry. The one judgment that could move it to ADD is a discount at the range floor, which the method card does not license without a dated catalyst.

Astra International is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates spanning vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property [S2]. It reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as three core businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3]. FY2025 parent net income split Automotive IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, heavy equipment and mining IDR9.10tn, agribusiness IDR1.17tn, infrastructure IDR1.26tn, IT IDR0.21tn and property IDR0.72tn [S4]. The 2026 strategy placed wider businesses under an earn-or-reallocate test [S11]; Jardine Cycle & Carriage controls 50.1% on a 43.0% free float [S6, S0]. The Others column is no longer a rounding item: nine-month attributable profit was IDR2.56tn, up more than a third, and the third quarter alone earned about half of that [S14, F71].

The October print is the delta, and the demand side is now read as well as the wholesale side. National wholesales reached 760,476 units over ten months and 81,482 in October, 31.2% on October 2025 and 2.4% on September, while retail sales reached 758,653 units over ten months and 82,429 in October alone, 29.3% on October 2025 and 1.5% on September [S20]. Two more months at October's pace leaves the full year a fraction below the top of the observers' 890,000 to 930,000 range and roughly a twelfth above the industry body's 850,000 target — effectively at the top, not away from it, and the prior text's "not at the top" was wrong [S20, S9, F101, F102, F138]. The 31.2% October growth is also against a weak October 2025 base of 62,090 units, so the monthly rate overstates the underlying trend even as it puts the year at the top of the range [S20, F104]. The monthly series reconciles: the ten-month total less the nine-month total implies a figure a few dozen units below the 81,482 the article reports for October, a rounding difference rather than an inconsistency [S20].

The comparatives in the October article are nine-month figures mislabelled as ten, and both are now corrected. The wholesale base of 561,405 equals the nine-month 2025 base implied by the nine-month 2026 print and its growth, and the retail base of 585,926 is within a few thousand units of the nine-month retail print [S20, F106, F124, F26, F112]. The restocking measure is now monthly, and October reverses it. Retail exceeded wholesale by 947 units in October, so the month was net destocking, not restocking [S20, F143]. Over the nine months of 2025 retail exceeded wholesale by more than twenty thousand units; over the nine months of 2026 wholesale now exceeds retail by a few thousand, roughly one unit in twenty-eight of wholesale [F124, F106, F26, F112]. That cumulative gap is now stale: the October month already unwound part of the swing the bear case names, so the restock reversal is a smaller residual risk for the fourth quarter than the cumulative measure implied, while the same print confirms dealers are drawing down stock into a cooling demand trend [S20, F139-F143]. We test the automotive mark against a retail-led volume path in the valuation and scenario sections.

Astra is losing share, and the report now says so. National car sales rose about a fifth to 679,000 over nine months while Astra's own car sales rose 13.0%, and Astra's group share is 49.0% against the 51.0% the company targeted for FY2025 [S14, S4, F14, F57, F125]. The automotive block carries the largest single weight in the sum of the parts, so a further two points of share loss is the largest single operating risk; its value effect is quantified in the valuation section and its place in the bear is set out with the scenarios. The motorcycle series is the demand base under the financing book rather than a consolidated revenue line: retail was 5,100,000 units over nine months, up 10.0% [S26].

The October print does not rescue the share story. Daihatsu, the group's own mass-market brand, sold 121,471 units retail in the ten months, 8.0% higher, with Gran Max alone at 62,377 [S28]; that trails the national retail market's 16.0% nine-month growth [S26]. Astra's four-wheel share was about 50.0% through August, and the company framed the rest of the year against a 850,000 GAIKINDO target [S30] that the October run-rate puts the full year above — the market grew faster than the industry body expected, not that Astra captured the growth. We keep the share-loss test as the automotive block's first operating break.

The mix is the structural story. LCGC wholesales were 83,997 units in the first nine months, a -11.0% change, about one car in eight against roughly one in six a year earlier [S18, F59]. ACC attributes the fall to buyers trading up with LCGC underwriting unchanged, which we treat as the primary cause because the group distributes the up-class nameplates too [S18]. The structural channel is Chinese electric models priced at LCGC levels: national EV wholesales reached 101,171 units in the first eight months, double the 50,749 a year earlier and almost the whole of FY2025's 103,931 [S9].

The mining complex turned in the third quarter. Over nine months Komatsu units fell to 3,000 and overburden to 766.0 million bank cubic metres; coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped [S14]. The division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted [S14].

The financing arm's own release reconciles cleanly, and the reconciliation is not a credit signal. Adira's new financing rose 13.0% to IDR35.10tn while managed receivables rose 7.0% to IDR65.80tn, and total revenue was IDR9.80tn with net profit of IDR1.60tn, up more than half [S26]. A book growing at roughly half the origination rate is the normal arithmetic of amortisation and prepayment on a portfolio that is not lengthening; the group shows the same pattern, with consumer financing receivables of IDR132.00tn against new financing of IDR92.50tn [S14, S26]. The credit evidence is improving rather than deteriorating: the gross non-performing ratio is 1.8% and provision expense fell 10.0% year on year [S26, F128, F129]. The two-company operational merger with Danamon and MUFG reached its operational go-live in October 2026 [S26].

Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles; the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm captive origination [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese and electrified entrants, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes shape demand [S14, S9]; the house macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, held back by the Martabe outage and the coal quota; the third quarter ran at a better margin as mining and gold recovered [S15, S14]. Selling and administrative expenses of IDR10.41tn and IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15]. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, of which IDR2.96tn was non-recurring impairment and fair-value charges; clean net profit was IDR24.57tn [S15, S14].

Two source labels are corrected. The 30 September 2026 accounts are **unaudited** — the filing says "tidak diaudit" — so the gearing, parent debt and book figures drawn from them are interim and only the FY2025 accounts carry an audit opinion [S15, S14, S6]. Capex is now the audited expenses-by-nature line of IDR18.46tn, not the data pack's IDR18,464.0bn, and it is no longer called an audited ratio on the data-pack figure [S6, F111, S0]. Depreciation is restated from the audited notes at IDR17.87tn for FY2025 and IDR16.70tn for FY2024 [S6]; FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, a margin of 17.5% [S6]. Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn, above consolidated profit as financing receivables grew [S15, S14].

Group net debt is restated from the filing, not the data pack. The audited cash balance of IDR52.62tn at 31 December 2025 puts FY2025 net debt at IDR57,680.0bn, which is the line the model now carries, in place of the lower data-pack figure the prior draft cited [S6, F118, S0]. Almost all of it sits in the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn at 30 September 2026, leaving group net cash of IDR1.80tn excluding them [S14]. The bridge uses parent-entity net debt — short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against cash of IDR2.64tn, plus lease liabilities of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S15] — so the group net-debt forecast does not drive the target.

**Actual versus forecast, on one basis.** The model is on a clean basis, and the text now says so. FY2026E net profit of IDR33,015.0bn is the clean nine months of IDR24.57tn plus an implied fourth quarter of roughly eight and a half trillion rupiah; the forecast's other income of IDR11,548.0bn is already the clean nine-month figure annualised, so the IDR2.96tn charge is excluded rather than added back [S15, S14, F48, F126]. The implied fourth quarter is roughly flat on the fourth quarter of 2025 — FY2025 profit of IDR32,769.0bn less the nine-month comparative of IDR24.47tn — so the step down from the third quarter is the ordinary seasonal pattern, not a forecast error. The prior draft added the charge back to a forecast that already excluded it and then compared the result with a clean base; that double count is removed and the "within a twentieth" claim is withdrawn [S14, F149].

The FY2026E EBITDA margin of 16.1% sits below the FY2025A 17.5% and the gap is answered here rather than left as a gate. It is the nine-month actual, not a forecast haircut: revenue was flat at IDR243.87tn while selling and general expenses of IDR10.41tn and IDR16.94tn rose, lifting the nine-month cost ratio to just over eleven per cent of revenue; the third quarter alone ran at just under eleven, and the year is carried at 11.1% against the audited 10.1% [S15, S6]. The prior text's ten-point-eight figure was the third-quarter rate mislabelled as the nine-month one; the nine-month figure is the higher of the two, and it is the one the forecast carries [S15]. The fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's better rate, so the year does not assume the nine-month pressure persists [S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate, and the cost ratio falls mechanically, not by assertion: costs grow with the macro deck's 3.3% inflation against 5.0% nominal revenue growth, a ratio factor of about ninety-eight and a half per cent a year, which takes 10.8% to the audited 10.1% and holds there [S15, S6, KB macro deck]. No LCGC-mix benefit and no cost-cut programme is assumed; real cost per unit of revenue stays at the last actual, which is the base-case discipline [S15, S6]. The minority take is 11.0% this year and 18.0% long run, toward the FY2025 audited rate as mining recovers [S15, S6]. Net income to the parent is IDR33,015.0bn, IDR34,009.0bn and IDR42,016.7bn [S15, S6].

Earnings quality, at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2023-FY2025 [S0] and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15]. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and stripped before the sum of the parts, while the P/E cross-check uses reported last-twelve-month earnings [S14, S0]. **Cost divergence** is real and we hold the nine-month ratio for the current year rather than bank operating leverage [S15]. **Financing provisioning** was built at IDR1.16tn in the first half against receivables of IDR132.00tn, but the nine-month trend is down, with the gross non-performing ratio at 1.8% and provision expense 10.0% lower year on year [S5, S26, F35, F60, F128, F129]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases of IDR84.94tn were about three tenths of cost and sales IDR27.94tn under a tenth of revenue, with no transfer-pricing test possible on consolidated accounts [S6]. **Revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum of the parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.6% and WACC 11.9%, from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.32 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.59), a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% and country risk of 2.5% [KB macro deck, 2026; house config].

**The marks now carry dates and floors.** The listed stakes go in at the 6 November 2026 close, not a stale pack price: United Tractors at Rp23,025 on the effective post-buyback 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari at Rp9,450 on 79.7% and Astra Graphia at Rp2,500 on 76.9% [S21, S22, S23, S6]. The automotive block is re-marked on a seasonal FY2026 income, not the third-quarter exit. The company's own FY2025 quarters show why: third-quarter 2025 auto income was IDR9.03tn less the first half's IDR5.40tn, about three and a half trillion rupiah, and the fourth quarter was IDR11.37tn less IDR9.03tn, about two and a third trillion — a fall of more than a third, a Q4/Q3 ratio of about two thirds [S14, S2, S4, F3, F147, F150]. Applying that ratio to the third quarter of 2026 — IDR9.79tn less the first half's IDR5.91tn — gives a fourth quarter of about two and a half trillion and FY2026 auto income of about twelve and a quarter trillion; at the section's seven and a third times that is about ninety trillion rupiah, not the hundred and fourteen the Q3 annualisation implied, roughly a fifth lower and about three hundred and seventy-five rupiah per share less after the discount [S14, S5, F32, F68]. October wholesales of 81,482 were in line with the Q3 monthly average, but 2025's own fourth quarter shows that a steady monthly rate does not carry the profit line [S20, S4]. The engine carries the mark as a nine and a quarter times scalar on the nine-month income of IDR9.79tn — the same value as seven and a third times the seasonal FY2026 figure — so the sourced nine-month fact drives it without a constructed forecast fact [S14, S15]. One Q4 convention now runs through the valuation: the lender is annualised on its nine-month income, the auto block is normalised on its own Q4/Q3 ratio, and mining is normalised off the Martabe-restart quarter [S15, S14].

The section multiple is the mean of Astra Otoparts' forward and Selamat Sempurna's last-twelve-month market P/E from the house data packs, disclosed as a forward/LTM mix and now bounded rather than asserted. The peer set is two component suppliers against an earnings base of Toyota and Daihatsu distribution plus the Honda motorcycle joint venture and Otoparts — not a like-for-like group, and there is no VAL_AUTOS house card, so the multiple is a disclosed approximation, not a precise mark [S19, S24, S25]. The mix effect is visible: on the same seasonal income the low peer multiple gives about eighty trillion and the high peer about a hundred trillion, a spread of roughly ten trillion rupiah or about a hundred rupiah per share after the discount, and the rating is HOLD at both ends [S24, S25]. AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November 2026 [S19], the later Yahoo close is a fraction below that and leaves the tender test unchanged [S24], and the SMSM price date is in the assumptions [S25]. The share-loss test: a further two points of share, from 49.0% to about forty-seven, is roughly a twentieth of the block's volume; against the automotive block's marked value that is about four and a half trillion rupiah of gross value, or about eighty rupiah per share after the discount — material but not thesis-breaking, and it is the bear's first operating break. The FY2025 division profit of IDR11.37tn is the earnings base the block is marked on, not the value lost [S14, F57, F125].

The financing block is on its own book/ROE card: income includes the segment's joint-venture results, so the book includes joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn against liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]. The return is the annualised actual, which already carries the first-half charge, and the block is carried at a justified premium to book because that return sits above the 14.6% cost of equity; the COE actually used in this block is the engine's 14.6%, not the fourteen point eight two the prior note quoted, and at that rate the justified P/B is about one and a fifth times book, which is the mark the engine carries [S0, S15]. The auto block uses a market multiple and no COE; the discount is applied after the roll. The prior draft haircut the return to sixteen per cent on no evidence, and Adira's own nine-month release contradicts the haircut, with provisions down 10.0% and the non-performing ratio at 1.8% [S26, F128, F129]. The downside is disclosed rather than modelled: a repeat of the first-half charge would take the return to the cost of equity and the mark to book, about a sixth of the block or roughly one hundred and ninety rupiah per share after the discount [S5, F35].

**The infrastructure block is now reconciled line by line, not left as a single floor.** Three figures must not be mixed. The IDR22.68tn is the book of the Others-column investments in joint ventures and associates — equity-method stakes, carried at book and marked there [S15, F123]. Astra Tol Nusantara is not inside that book: it is a wholly owned, consolidated toll operator with IDR24.85tn of total assets [S15, F122], so its assets sit in the consolidated balance sheet rather than in the equity-method investment line, and the two figures do not overlap — adding them would count different things, not double count the same thing. The directly held concession rights of PT Marga Harjaya and PT Marga Mandalasakti are a separate intangible on the consolidated balance sheet at IDR9.51tn [S15, F146]; they are additive to the equity-method book and are marked at book. Serasi Autoraya, the logistics business, is not in this block at all: its IDR8.59tn of total assets are disclosed in the automotive group structure and its earnings sit inside the automotive segment, so it is already carried in the automotive mark and would be double counted if added here [S15, F145].

The engine therefore carries two infrastructure holdings, the equity-method book of IDR22.68tn and the concession-rights floor of IDR9.51tn, about twenty-three and nine and a half trillion rupiah respectively [S15, F123, F146]. ATN's own equity is not disclosed separately — the segment note gives only its total assets — so we do not invent a book equity for it, and ATN's residual net assets beyond the IDR9.51tn of directly held concession rights — its own working capital and cash — are carried at nil, disclosed as a limitation rather than valued. The marks capitalise no ATN earnings: the IDR22.68tn book capitalises the associate stakes, and the nine-month Others profit of IDR2.56tn is segment context, not a valuation input [S15, F71, F122, F146]. The prior draft's error was to treat its assets as excluded value while leaving the concession rights at zero. Restoring the concession rights to the mark adds about one hundred and fifty rupiah per share after the discount; the combined book mark is a floor on both counts, because the segment note splits neither the joint-venture book nor the healthcare and digital businesses out of the Others column [S15, F123].

Property is marked on the listed subsidiary's market value, and the false claim is deleted. MMLP closed at Rp214 on 6 November 2026 [S27, F119], which capitalises its IDR6.48tn of total assets at a fraction of book; the same ratio applied to Menara Astra's IDR26.48tn of consolidated assets, which include the MMLP holding, gives the block's mark, and Astra Land is carried inside it [S15, S27, F120, F121]. The prior draft said no MMLP data pack existed in coverage; that was false, MMLP is in coverage, and the mark is now anchored on its traded price rather than on a residual behind its earnings [S27]. The effect is about seventy-five rupiah per share. Parent G&A sits inside the automotive mark because the parent is an operating distributor [S15].

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: P/E gives Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, 26.9% and 56.4% above the sum of the parts [S0]. They are undiscounted while the parts carry a 35% discount, P/BV uses the 30 September book of IDR238.10tn [S15], and the averages were struck when mining earned far more — H1-2025 mining profit was IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn a year later [S5].

**The bridge line is display-only and reconciles to the filing.** The consolidated net-debt line shown in the bridge is the filed 30 September 2026 figure of IDR64.92tn, cross-checked as financing-services net debt of IDR66.70tn less ex-financing-services net cash of IDR1.80tn [S15, S14, F100, F51, F50]. No method applies it: the sum of the parts deducts parent-entity net debt only — IDR5.05tn of short-term borrowings against IDR2.64tn of cash, plus lease liabilities of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S15] — and the P/E and P/BV cross-checks are direct equity values, so the line changes neither the target nor the rating.

**The discount is the base rate, and the peer set is shown in full.** The base holds 35%, the midpoint between the name's own peer level and the peer median, applied to the marks and independent of the share price. The card says holdco discounts persist indefinitely by default and that cheapness alone is not a thesis. The full CONGLOMERATES set, as house assumptions of the analysts who cover those names rather than as observed market discounts, runs from ABMM near seven tenths and ZBRA at two thirds, through IMJS at three fifths and a cluster at two fifths (BHIT, FOLK, DSSA, TOBA), to BNMR at thirty-eight per cent, JKON at thirty-five, five names at thirty including Astra, and PACK and TSPC below that [cov_publish comps]. The median is just under two fifths, and two fifths excluding Astra, so the base of 35% sits below the peer median but above the name's own level in the set: the peer figures are other analysts' house assumptions, not observed market discounts, and the median is pulled up by small caps whose discount embeds liquidity and governance this name does not share [cov_publish comps]. The card also asks for the name's own five-year discount-to-NAV history: it cannot be built, because no historical sum-of-parts NAV exists in the record and the house has not published one for this name; the closest own series is P/B, which has averaged 1.1x over FY2022A-FY2025A and stands below book on the 30 September equity of IDR238.10tn [S0, S15]. We hold the midpoint between the name's own level and the peer median rather than either end, because two name-specific facts argue for a wider discount than Astra's own thirty per cent rather than a narrower one — no dated narrowing catalyst, the authorised buyback having no end date or pace [S8, S14, S16], and related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn, a structural and untested flow [S6]. The choice is shown, not hidden: at two fifths the target is about eight per cent below the price after the roll, at thirty-five about flat, at thirty about seven per cent above, and only at the twenty-five per cent floor does it clear the ten per cent add_min line, at about fourteen per cent [S0]. The HOLD is therefore not a knife-edge on the discount; it survives the whole thirty-to-forty band, and the call would need the floor — and the dated catalyst the card requires — to become ADD. Upstream cover is above one, with parent profit of IDR19.89tn against IDR16.43tn of dividends paid, so the discount is not argued from dividend distress [S6, F98, F22].

**Target construction, and the roll shown separately.** The base compounds the blended mark of Rp4,347 at the 14.6% cost of equity and nets Rp399 of dividends, giving Rp4,584; weighting base 45%, bear 30% at Rp4,270 and bull 25% at Rp4,894 gives Rp4,567 [S15, S0]. The roll is a template convention, not a thesis: un-rolled, the blended mark of Rp4,347 plus the Rp399 dividend is about five per cent below the Rp5,000 price on its own, and the one-year roll at the cost of equity moves the expected return to -0.7% — a HOLD either way. The ten per cent add_min threshold is not met on the un-rolled basis or the rolled one, and the target stays below the price after the roll, which is why the rating is HOLD [S0]. There is no discount-convergence term, and no dated catalyst is underwritten. The weights are probabilities of the discount path, not of the operating path, and the scenario section says what that leaves out.

**What the price implies.** At Rp5,000 the market capitalises the parts at a 24.0% discount, inside the card's twenty-to-forty per cent range but near its narrow end, not its midpoint. That is the fair place for a holdco with no dated catalyst to sit, and it is why the target of Rp4,567 is -8.7% below the price, with an expected return of -0.7%: we hold the base rate, and the cost-of-equity roll does not lift the target back through the price. The FY2025 multiple is 0.9x on the audited book, and the shares stand below book on the 30 September equity of IDR238.10tn [S0, S15] — a cheapness signal, not a catalyst.

**The scenario engine has a disclosed limit, and the table is labelled for it.** The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals in every case, so the bear's revenue, margin and share-count shocks do not reprice the parts. The tabulated bear and bull are therefore discount-path values, and the probabilities attached to them are probabilities of the discount path: base 45%, bear 30%, bull 25% [S15, S14]. The operating content of each tail is quantified here instead, because the engine cannot carry it. The bear's four operating breaks are: a further two points of car share, about eighty rupiah per share [S14, F57, F125]; a reversal of the restocking swing, roughly one unit in twenty-eight of nine-month wholesale, which would take the automotive block's volume back toward retail [S20, F26, F112, F124]; a mining non-recovery, with coal and gold at the nine-month run-rate rather than the restart quarter [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; and a credit break from an improving trend, a repeat of the first-half charge taking the financing mark to book, about a sixth of the block or roughly one hundred and ninety rupiah per share [S5, F35, S26, F128, F129]. The bull's operating content is the mirror: share back to 51.0%, the coal quota reset, and costs held at the nine-month ratio rather than glided down [S14, S18]. The Others and infrastructure run-rate is not bull-only, because the base now marks that block at the 30 September book [S15, F123]. On our own arithmetic those operating breaks sum to roughly two hundred and eighty to three hundred rupiah per share, so the tabulated bear at Rp4,270 — a discount-path value that holds the listed stakes at market — understates the operating downside by about that amount; read the bear as the discount tail and add the operating breaks separately, rather than treating the table as the full downside [S15, S5, S26]. We say this plainly instead of bridging a hidden operating bear into the engine.

**The rating does not depend on the weights.** Doubling the bear weight to three fifths, with three tenths base and a tenth bull, gives a weighted target of about four and four-tenths thousand rupiah and a total return of about minus three and a half per cent — still HOLD [S0]. What would move the call is evidence, not a weight: a dated end to the buyback so that completion pace becomes a catalyst, a dividend step-up or an asset sale that upstreams cash, share data showing Astra holding share through the restocking unwind, or a peer discount observed in transactions rather than in other analysts' house assumptions [S8, S14, S16, S20].

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever, and coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings [S14, S9, S4].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and is cautious on rate-sensitive Indonesian demand [KB macro deck, 2026]; a consumer-financing group is exposed on both demand and credit, and that caution sits in the country risk premium [S2, S4].

**Competitive and technology risk — high likelihood, material impact.** Chinese and electrified entrants threaten the auto franchise, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; the share series has already moved from 51.0% to 49.0% in the actuals, so this is a trend, not a tail [S9, S14, F14, F57, F125].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block carries IDR66.70tn of net debt against receivables of IDR132.00tn. The trend is currently improving, with the gross non-performing ratio at 1.8% and provisions down 10.0%, so the risk is a break in that trend rather than a continuation of stress; a repeat of the IDR1.16tn first-half charge inside one quarter would cut the block's return to the cost of equity and the mark to book, and the engine does not reprice the mark in a scenario [S5, S14, S26, F35, F128, F129].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8].
**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR244.7bn a day, parent profit covered the FY2025 dividend, and the interim held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10].

The base (45%) carries the actual nine months, the Q3 auto exit, the nine-month cost ratio gliding to the audited ratio, a minority take near the audited level, the discount at 35% with no narrowing, and buyback retirement at the completed pace [S14, S20]; it gives Rp4,584. The bull (25%) assumes Astra's share recovers toward the company's 51.0% target, the coal quota resets, costs stay at the nine-month ratio, and the discount narrows to the floor of the card range [S14, S11, S18]. The bear (30%) is the discount-path case — a discount back to the peer median — with the four operating breaks above carried alongside it in the text, not inside the engine target [S14, S5, S9, S26]. The discount shocks are mirrored; the probabilities are not, because the narrowing catalyst is undated and the share trend is already negative.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Buyback execution at the completed pace through the authorised amount, a dated capital-allocation event that upstreams cash, October-November share data showing Astra holding its share, retail sales keeping pace with wholesale so the restocking swing unwinds without a volume cut, and financing provisioning that stays on the improving nine-month trend rather than rising [S14, S20, S5, S26].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group, on a 43.0% free float [S0, S6]; no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed [S6]. Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn and sales IDR27.94tn, principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures; the purchase ratio fell from 32.8% of cost while the gross margin held, but the consolidated accounts do not permit a transfer-pricing test, so the flow is structural and untested — a discount-widening fact, not a clean bill [S6]. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026 and the IDR8.00tn programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. The Otoparts tender at Rp3,600 for up to 4.95 per cent lifts the stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November 2026, so the offer is a small transfer from the parent to minorities [S19]. On the financing side, Adira reached the operational go-live in October 2026 of its merger with Mandala Finance, a step inside the Danamon and MUFG group that controls both lenders rather than a merger with them, which is a control-and-integration item to monitor rather than a value event on its own [S26]. On ESG the material exposures are coal, palm oil, nickel and the vehicle transition, met through Japanese partners rather than a platform the group owns [S14, S9].

**Audit, listing status and related-party gravity.** The FY2025 accounts carry no audit opinion in the archived text: the auditor's report pages are blank and no audit firm is named, so we record the accounts as carrying no readable opinion rather than as audited-clean, and we have not established the auditor's identity from any source we hold [S6]. No source states the IDX board or a special notation; we read the FY2025 accounts and the nine-month 2026 release and found no special-monitoring-board disclosure or notation letter, which is an absence of evidence, not a clean bill, and it is recorded as an open check rather than resolved [S6, S15]. Related-party gravity is quantified at both levels: purchases of IDR84.94tn were a quarter of FY2025 revenue and about a sixth of consolidated total assets of IDR507.37tn, and sales of IDR27.94tn were under a tenth of revenue and about a twentieth of assets [S6, F20, F21, F148]. These are optics-class structural flags, not confirmed manipulation: the flows are disclosed and principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures, but the purchase flow is large enough to widen the warranted holdco discount, and it is one of the two name-specific facts behind the base discount [S6, F21].

The dated catalysts are the Otoparts tender close, the monthly wholesale data and the FY2026 audited results, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S13, S20, S4]. None is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst, which is why the base holds the midpoint discount and the rating is HOLD [S8, S14].

We monitor the ten-month run-rate of 760,476 and Astra's monthly share, last stated at about 50.0% through August [S20, S30, F57]; Daihatsu's retail pace against the market, 8.0% over ten months against 16.0% over nine [S28, S26]; the gap between wholesale and retail, which is the restocking swing [S20, F26, F112]; the LCGC versus up-class split [S18]; Komatsu units and overburden [S14]; financing receivables, the non-performing ratio and provisioning [S14, S26]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and parent profit against dividends paid [S6].

bear.narrative: Four operating breaks, each with its measured size, and a discount back to the peer median. (1) AUTO SHARE AND MIX: Astra's share already fell from 51% in FY2025 to 49% over nine months 2026, and its own car sales rose 13% against a market up 21% [S14, F14, F57, F125, F59]; a further two-point loss to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9] at the 7.357x section multiple removes about a twenty-fifth of the auto block, roughly Rp4.6tn before the discount. (2) RESTOCK REVERSAL: nine-month wholesale of 679,020 now exceeds retail of 676,000, after retail exceeded wholesale by about 21,400 units a year earlier [S14, F26, F112, F124, F106] - about 24,400 units, 3.6% of nine-month wholesale, is dealer restocking rather than end demand, and a retail-led fourth quarter gives it back. (3) MINING: the national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. (4) CREDIT: the financing book's evidence has been improving, not deteriorating - gross NPF 1.8%, impairment provision expense down 10% year on year [S26, F128, F129] - so the bear is a break from that trend, not its continuation: a repeat of the Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge inside one quarter against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60] takes the block's return to about the cost of equity and the mark from 1.21x to 1.0x book, about Rp10.8tn or a sixth of the block. The buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the ~40% peer median, from the 35% base [S8, S14], a mirrored 5pp move. Disclosed limit: the holdco_sotp engine reprices neither the marks nor the discount inside a holding, so the table carries the discount and the earnings weight only; the four operating breaks above are quantified here and in section 5, not in the tabulated bear. Their total is several times the tabulated gap and is not used to justify the bear's 30% weight. We state plainly that the published bear therefore UNDERSTATES the operating downside by roughly Rp280-300 per share beyond the tabulated discount path: UNTR is 18% of gross value and is held at the 6 November close in every case, so the named mining non-recovery has zero value effect in the table.

bull.narrative: Three operating breaks and a mirrored discount. (1) AUTO SHARE: ten-month wholesales reached 760,476 units and October ran at 81,482 [S20, F101, F102], and the bull's incremental assumption is that Astra's 49% share recovers to the 51% it earned in FY2025 [S14, F57, F14] rather than that the market beats its range, with Astra taking the up-class volume it is already selling [S18]; two points of share back at the 7.357x section multiple adds roughly the Rp4.6tn the bear removes. (2) MINING: the national coal quota resets and the complex stabilises - a bull assumption, not in the base - with the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap [S11]. (3) COST AND MIX: share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin and the opex ratio holds at the third quarter's 10.84% instead of gliding to the audited 10.14% [S15, S6]. (4) DISCOUNT: the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount from the 35% base to 30%, Astra's own level in the house peer set - we do not assume a break below it without a dated catalyst, and the undated buyback is not one [S8, S14, S16]. The bull narrows the discount by 5pp, the mirror of the bear. The Others/infrastructure run-rate is NOT a bull-only item: the base marks that block at the 30 September book, which already carries the nine-month Others profit of Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S14, F71]. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) sits outside the table because it is a transfer inside an already consolidated block. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue. From FY2027E the ratio glides from the third quarter's 10.84% actual to the FY2025 audited 10.14% [S6]: the nine-month 11.22% is depressed by the Martabe outage, which cut revenue (the same base effect the 21.3% nine-month gross margin shows), and the third quarter - after the gold restart and the coal-volume recovery - already ran at 10.84% [S15, S14]. Holding 11.22% to FY2035 would mean costs growing at revenue growth in perpetuity, a permanent step-up of about Rp3.2tn a year of EBIT against the audited ratio, which is an unsourced conservative drift, not the last actual. The glide is mechanical, not a forecast: costs grow with the macro deck's inflation (3.28%) against 5% nominal revenue [KB macro deck], a ratio factor of 0.984 a year, so the ratio falls from 10.84% to 10.66%, 10.49% and 10.32% over FY2028E-FY2030E and converges to the audited 10.14% in the long run. Real cost per unit of revenue is therefore held at the last actual, which is what the base-case card asks for.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual from the expenses-by-nature note, capex Rp18,464bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn, or 5.71% [S6, F111]; the data pack's Rp17,440bn is a different capex definition and is not used now that the audited line is sourced. The group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised further.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E the take rises to 17% and 18% long run, close to the FY2025 audited 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]): the base has mining recovering (gross margin back to the FY2025 audited rate and revenue growing), so a mining recovery must lift the minority share toward - not away from - the last audited level. The wholly owned auto and financing mix keeps the long-run take just below that 18.5% actual, not at the 15% used before, which assumed the mining recovery accrued disproportionately to the parent. The UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and share count.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -4.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM [S8, S16] is carried to completion at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65], which is about Rp0.9tn a month. Rp8tn at that pace retires about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the 39.69bn count, in roughly nine months, inside FY2027E. The prior 2.0% truncated the programme after one year for no sourced reason and understated the only holdco-level capital return the company is actually executing; the remaining uncertainty is timing, not the pace, and the bull carries no extra retirement.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 35%, the midpoint between Astra's own level in the house CONGLOMERATES peer set (30%, one of five names including Astra) and the peer median (just under two fifths, ~39-40%, lifted by small or illiquid names at 60-70% such as ABMM, ZBRA and IMJS) [cov_publish comps]. It is also the next name up in the peer set, JKON at 35%. The red team is right that the two name-specific facts point WIDER than 30%: there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM carries no end date or disclosed pace [S8, S14, S16]) and related-party purchases were Rp84.9tn, about a quarter of FY2025 revenue, a structural and untested flow that the method card says widens the warranted discount [S6, F21]. Those facts justify moving from 30% up to 35%, not down; we do not import the full small-cap median into a blue-chip with a mostly-listed NAV marked at market. Upstream cover is above one on the parent's own accounts - FY2025 profit for the year of Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22] - so the discount is not argued from dividend distress. The discount is independent of the share price: the target is an output of the marks and this discount, not a reproduction of the 6 November close [S0]. The published bear carries the ~40% peer median and the bull Astra's own 30%; the rating is shown in section 4 at 25/30/35/40% so the reader can see it turns REDUCE only at the peer median.

challenges.challenge: The automotive block, 41% of gross SOTP value, is marked on the Q3 quarter annualised (11.6456 x 9,787 = 113,975bn, i.e. 7.357x on 15,492bn) on the assertion that the Q3 exit is the current run-rate rather than a spike. The company's own quarters contradict it: Q3-2025 auto income was 3,629 (9M 9,033 less H1 5,404) and Q4-2025 was 2,332 (FY 11,365 less 9M 9,033), a -36% seasonal fall. A seasonal Q4-2026 (Q4-2025 x 21% market growth, about 2,820) gives FY2026 auto income of about 12,610, so 7.357x is 92,770bn not 113,975bn: the block is overstated by about 21,200bn, or about 375/share after the 30% discount. That alone takes the base SOTP to about 4,459 and TR to about 3.7%, i.e. HOLD. The treatment is also inconsistent: mining Q4 is normalised and finserv is annualised on 9M, only auto gets the Q3 uplift [S15, S5, S4, F68, F32, F77].
challenges.answer: Auto block re-marked on a seasonal FY2026 income: FY2025 quarters give Q3 3,629 and Q4 2,332, a 0.643 ratio, applied to Q3-2026 3,873 gives FY2026E about 12,276 and, at the section multiple, about 90,315 versus 113,975 on the Q3 annualisation; the engine carries it as 9.23x the nine-month fact and the rating is HOLD [S14, S5, S4, F3, F32, F147, F150].

challenges.challenge: The actual-versus-forecast paragraph is arithmetically false. FY2026E other_nonop is 11,548, which is exactly the clean nine-month other income (JV 8,127 less other expense 2,429 plus the 2,963 addback = 8,661) x 4/3, so the forecast already excludes the Rp2.96tn charge; adding it back double counts. On the model's own lines the implied Q4 is 33,015 - 24,565 = 8,450 clean, which is 30% below Q3's clean 12,032, not within a twentieth. The claim that the auto Q3 exit and the profit line are consistent therefore fails on its own arithmetic [S15, S14, F48, F126].
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states the model is on a clean basis: other income already equals the clean nine months annualised, the implied Q4 is about 8,450 against 8,296 in Q4-2025 (+1.9%), and the double count and the within-a-twentieth claim are withdrawn [S15, S14, F48, F149].

challenges.challenge: The 30% holdco discount is the single largest value judgment and sits below the house peer median the report itself tabulates (~40%, just under two fifths and two fifths excluding Astra). The two name-specific facts cited for not using the peer median - no dated narrowing catalyst and a 26.3%-of-revenue related-party purchase flow (84,937/323,392) - argue for a WIDER discount, not a narrower one, so the rationale contradicts the choice. At 40% the SOTP is 4,144 and the base TR is about -3% (HOLD). No own five-year discount-to-NAV history is produced, so 30% is a generic midpoint doing about 6.5% of target work [S0, S6, F21, F3].
challenges.answer: Discount raised to 35%, the midpoint between Astra 30% and the peer median just under 40%; the text shows the target at 25/30/35/40, states HOLD survives the 30-40 band and ADD appears only at the floor; peer figures are other analysts house assumptions and the median is pulled up by small caps [cov_publish comps, S0].

challenges.challenge: The ADD is entirely the one-year COE roll. The base SOTP is 4,834, 3.3% BELOW the 5,000 price; the target is v0 x (1+COE) - DPS, so the un-rolled expected return is (4,834 + 399)/5,000 - 1 = 5.6%, which is HOLD. The 11.2% clears the 10% add_min threshold by 1.2pp, and the report concedes there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst, which VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rules 2-3 and data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing require before underwriting a discount-path call (a cheap discount alone is not a thesis) [S0, S8, S14].
challenges.answer: The roll is now shown separately: un-rolled, the blended mark plus the dividend is about five per cent below the price, a HOLD on its own; the roll takes it to minus 0.7%, the 10% add_min line is not met on either basis, and no dated narrowing catalyst is underwritten [S0, S8].

challenges.challenge: The published bear (4,486 at 30%) is a discount-only path, not an operating bear. The holdco_sotp engine holds UNTR at the 6 November close (49,962bn, 18% of gross value) in every scenario, so the named mining non-recovery break has zero value effect; the auto share break, the restock reversal and the credit break are quantified in the text but never applied to the bear target. The bear v0 of 4,220 is the 40% discount case alone (6,906 x 0.6 = 4,144 plus the 4% earnings weight), so the tabulated downside omits about 280-300/share of breaks the report itself measures [S15, F108, S5, S26].
challenges.answer: Section 5 states explicitly that the published bear, which holds the listed stakes at market, understates the operating downside by roughly 280-300 per share after the discount; the four operating breaks are quantified alongside the table [S15, F108, S5, S26].

challenges.challenge: The infrastructure mark is 22,679bn, the book of the Others-column investments in JVs and associates, and the note concedes it excludes PT Astra Tol Nusantara's own consolidated toll assets (total assets Rp24,853bn), PT Marga Mandalasakti, PT Marga Harjaya, and the Serasi Autoraya logistics business. A 100%-owned operating toll operator and a 100%-owned logistics business are therefore valued at zero. That is an omission, not a floor. The report also says ATN's assets are inside the consolidated accounts rather than in the stake book, which raises the second question: if ATN's 24,853 includes the 22,679 of JV stakes, the two figures overlap and the 22,679 may double count part of ATN [S15, F122, F123].
challenges.answer: Infrastructure is reconciled: 22,679 is the equity-method JV/associate book, ATN is a 100%-owned consolidated operator whose 24,853 total assets do not overlap or add to it, the 9,509 concession rights are additive and now marked at book, and Serasi sits in the automotive block [S15, F122, F123, F146, F145].

challenges.challenge: The event's demand-side half is missing. S20 reports October retail sales of 82,429, up 29.3% year on year and 1.5% on September, and explicitly notes retail was 947 units ABOVE wholesale in the month (Retail Sales Lebih Tinggi dari Wholesales). The report cites only wholesale 81,482 and reads the month as confirmation of the Q3 auto exit while keeping restocking as a live bear risk. October is in fact net destocking, so the cumulative one-unit-in-twenty-eight measure (a 9M swing against 9M2025) is stale and the bear's retail-led fourth quarter break has partly already happened, which cuts against the report's framing in both directions [S20, F101, F102, F26, F112].
challenges.answer: Section 2 adds October retail 82,429, up 29.3% yoy and 1.5% mom, 947 units above wholesale; the gap is now read monthly, October is net destocking, and the text says the residual restock reversal is smaller while confirming dealers drawing down stock [S20, F139-F143].

challenges.challenge: Two drifts away from the last actual are unexplained. (1) Calibration: FY2026E EBITDA margin is 16.1% against the FY2025A actual of 17.5% (gap -1.38pp, a WARN, not justified in qc_justifications), driven by opex at 11.12% of revenue vs 10.14% audited; the 9M ratio is a genuine source but the report never states the gap or answers the gate. (2) From FY2027E opex glides from 11.1% to 10.1% and holds, worth about 3.3tn of EBIT, on the asserted reason of a smaller low-margin LCGC mix - but LCGC volume fell 11% and the mix claim is not measured against any sourced margin-per-unit [S15, S6, S18].
challenges.answer: Calibration gap 16.1% vs 17.5% is answered in the text and in qc_justifications: it is the nine-month actual cost ratio on flat revenue during the Martabe outage, not a haircut; the FY2027 glide is arithmetic, cost inflation 3.28% against 5% revenue growth, with the LCGC-mix claim removed [S15, S6, S14].

challenges.challenge: The largest unlisted block is valued on a section multiple of 7.357x that is the mean of Astra Otoparts' forward P/E (6.55x) and Selamat Sempurna's LTM P/E (8.17x) - two component suppliers - applied to a distribution-plus-JV earnings base (Toyota/Daihatsu distribution, Astra Honda Motor, Otoparts). VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT rule 1 requires unlisted segments on their own house card and forbids a blanket multiple; there is no VAL_AUTOS card, and a forward/LTM mix across two different businesses is not a coherent peer set. The report discloses the mix but does not test it [S15, F68, S19, S24, S25].
challenges.answer: The peer set is disclosed as two component suppliers against a distribution-plus-JV earnings base, no VAL_AUTOS card exists, and the mix is bounded: about 80,408 at 6.55x and 100,295 at 8.17x, a spread of about 100 per share after the discount, with HOLD at both ends [S19, S24, S25].

challenges.challenge: Three internal numbers do not reconcile. (1) Section 3 says costs glide from the nine-month 10.8% to the audited 10.1% while the assumptions and the same paragraph give the nine-month selling-plus-G&A ratio as 11.22% (27,353/243,869) and the FY2026E input as 11.12%. (2) The finserv note calls 14.82% the engine COE when the engine COE is 14.63%; at 14.63% the justified P/B is 1.212x, lifting the finserv mark by about Rp20/share. (3) S20's 10M 760,476 less the 9M 679,020 implies October of 81,456, not the 81,482 reported [S15, S6, S20].
challenges.answer: All three reconcile: the nine-month cost ratio is 11.22% while the third quarter is 10.84% and FY2026E 11.12%; the finserv block uses the engine COE 14.63% with justified P/B 1.212x; October implied 81,456 versus 81,482 reported is a rounding difference [S15, S0, S20].

challenges.challenge: Three discount-widening facts are filed as open checks rather than risks. The FY2025 accounts carry blank pages where the auditor's report sits and name no audit firm; no IDX board or notation is stated; and related-party purchases of 84,937 (26.3% of revenue) are given only as about three tenths of cost. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS requires the related-party percentage of revenue and assets and treats auditor opacity and any special notation as flags at both levels. The report says it found nothing, but has not looked at the auditor's identity or the board status [S6, F21, F20].
challenges.answer: Governance now records the FY2025 accounts as carrying no readable audit opinion, no audit firm named and no IDX board or notation found, as an open check; related-party purchases are 26.3% of revenue and 16.7% of assets, sales 8.6% and 5.5% [S6, F20, F21, F148].

challenges.challenge: Two more months at October's pace puts the full year inside the observers' 890,000 to 930,000 range, not at the top of it: 760,476 + 2 x 81,482 = 923,440, which is 99.3% of the range top and 8.6% above the 850,000 Gaikindo target - effectively at the top, not away from it. The October +31.2% is also against a weak October 2025 base of 62,090, which the text does not note [S20, F102, F104].
challenges.answer: Run-rate now stated as effectively at the top: two more months at October pace gives about 923,440, 99.3% of the range top and 8.6% above the GAIKINDO target, and the text notes October +31.2% is against a weak 62,090 base [S20, F102, F104, F138].

challenges.challenge: The rating does not survive the checklist's own probability test. Doubling the bear weight (to 60%, base 30%, bull 10%) gives a weighted target of 4,842 and a total return of 4.8%, i.e. HOLD; the reported 11.2% is 1.2pp above the 10% add_min threshold. Combined with C1 and C3, whose single-judgment changes each take TR to about 3.7% and -3%, the ADD has no margin of safety on any of the three inputs it depends on [S0].
challenges.answer: Section 5 shows the doubled-bear weights: 60% bear, 30% base, 10% bull gives a weighted target of about 4,426 and TR of about minus 3.5%, still HOLD; the text names the evidence that would move the call and does not present the return as robust [S0, S14, S16].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 "What the price implies" still says "it is why the target is only modestly above the price" and calls the market-implied discount "near its midpoint". The target 4,567 is 8.7% BELOW the 5,000 price with TR -0.7%, and 24.0% (1 - 198,455 / 261,065) sits near the NARROW end of the 20-40% card range, not its 30% midpoint. The paragraph states the reverse of the call in a note whose whole conclusion is "target below price, hence HOLD", and contradicts Section 4 own later sentence that the target stays below the price after the roll.
challenges.answer: Rewrote both sentences in What the price implies: the {{val.tp_final|px}} target is {{val.upside_pct|pctv}} below the {{mkt.last_price|px}} price, expected return {{val.tr_pct|pctv}}, and the {{rev.implied_value|pct}} implied discount now reads near the narrow end of the twenty-to-forty per cent range, not its midpoint. Removed the modestly-above-price and roll-plus-dividend claims.

challenges.challenge: The signed bias audit still reads "It is conservative in two: the 35% base sits below the peer median". A discount BELOW the ~40% peer median is the more OPTIMISTIC choice on value, not the conservative one: at 40% the target is ~4,221 and TR ~-8%, at 30% ~4,945 and +7%. The signed audit therefore reverses the direction of the single largest value judgment, in the same text that shows the 25/30/35/40 sensitivity and calls the peer median "just under two fifths". This is the bias area the red team and the judge both flagged.
challenges.answer: Relabelled the discount in the signed bias audit as optimistic against the just-under-two-fifths peer median and conservative only against Astra own thirty per cent level; the discount sensitivity from the floor to two fifths still shows the HOLD survives the band. The 35% assumption is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The packet and review bridge line still carries consolidated net debt of 63,049 against the filed 30 September 2026 figure of 64,925 [S15, F100] (cross-check: finserv 66,700 less ex-finserv net cash 1,800 [S14, F51, F50]). QC Q1 found this and it is unfixed; it is also the line that led the judge to a BLOCK. It is display-only and applied to no method, but a published valuation record that does not reconcile to the filing is not signable.
challenges.answer: Added a bridge paragraph in Section 4 restating the display line to the filed 30 September 2026 consolidated net debt of {{fact.F100|idrtn}}, cross-checked as finserv {{fact.F51|idrtn}} less ex-finserv net cash {{fact.F50|idrtn}}, and labelled it display-only: no method applies it because the SOTP deducts parent net debt only.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says Astra Tol Nusantara "value is carried through the Others segment earnings that the stake book and the nine-month Others profit of 2,558 capture", while the mark is the 22,679 book of equity-method stakes, which capitalises no earnings, and ATN residual net assets beyond the 9,509 concession rights are carried at nil. The paragraph both says no book equity is invented for ATN and claims its value arrives through earnings, so the reader cannot tell what the toll assets are worth. QC Q5 required the prose to match the mark.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the ATN paragraph to state plainly that ATN residual net assets beyond the {{fact.F146|idrtn}} of concession rights (working capital, cash) are carried at nil, and removed the claim that the book stake or the Others profit captures ATN earnings, which it does not.

missing_bull_case.note: Two owned assets and the demand-side print are missing: the 100%-owned Astra Tol Nusantara (total assets 24,853) and Serasi Autoraya are excluded from the infrastructure mark and valued at zero [S15, F122], and S20's October retail figure (82,429, +29.3% yoy, 947 units above wholesale) is never cited even though it is the only demand-side read in the event [S20].

missing_bear_case.note: The published bear (4,486) is a discount-only path: the engine holds UNTR at the 6 November market price, so the named mining non-recovery break (UNTR is 18% of gross SOTP value) has zero valuation effect, and the four operating breaks the text quantifies are not applied to the bear target [S15, F108]. The audit gap (blank auditor pages, no board or notation named) and the 26.3%-of-revenue related-party purchase flow are discount-widening facts filed as open checks, not risks [S6, F21].

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are not all realistic. The auto block (41% of gross value) is marked on Q3 x 4 = 15,492 when the company's own FY2025 quarters put Q3 auto income at 3,629 and Q4 at 2,332 (-36%), so a seasonal build gives about 12.2-12.6tn; the P&L's own Q4 (8,450 clean) is 30% below Q3; and the FY2027 opex glide to 10.1% is asserted against a 9M2026 actual of 11.22% with no measured driver [S15, S5, S4, S14].

evidence_and_citations.note: Most load-bearing facts trace cleanly (October print, segment profits, 48% payout, 62.12% effective UNTR stake, 1,160 H1 provision, 22,679 JV book all verified verbatim), but the section 3 reported-basis statement is false against the analyst's own assumptions, and three numbers do not reconcile: 10.8% vs 11.22% opex, 14.82% vs 14.63% COE, and October 81,456 implied vs 81,482 reported [S15, S20, S6].

valuation_method_fit.note: SOTP is the right primary and the marks are dated, but the discount (30%) is 10pp below the house peer median (~40%) the report itself tabulates and the name-specific facts cited argue for a wider, not narrower, discount; there is no dated narrowing catalyst, which the card and base_rates require; and the largest unlisted block uses a blanket multiple from two component suppliers, which rule 1 forbids [S0, S15].

bias_and_tone.note: The prose over-corrects in places ('not at the top of the range' when the run-rate is 99.3% of the top) and, more importantly, the ADD is the one-year COE roll: base SOTP 4,834 sits 3.3% below the 5,000 price and the un-rolled return is 5.6% (HOLD). The 11.2% clears the 10% add_min line by 1.2pp and doubling the bear weight flips the call [S0].

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck inputs are read consistently: COE 14.63% from the KB macro deck (rf 7.45%, spread 1.62%, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%), g 4% under the 5% cap, and peer holdco discounts from house CONGLOMERATES coverage rather than market observation. Only defect is the finserv note calling 14.82% the engine COE when the engine uses 14.63% (see C10) [S0].

conservatism_audit.note: The stack is optimistic at four points: the Q3-exit auto mark (about +375/share vs a seasonal build), the 30% discount vs the 40% peer median (about +345/share), the FY2027 share change of -4.0% from an Rp8tn programme with no disclosed end date or pace, and the FY2027-31 opex glide. The genuinely conservative items (capex at the audited 18,464; payout at the company's 48%; infra at a book floor) are at or below the last actual and sourced [S6, S4, S15].

calibration.note: No BLOCK flags, but the calibration WARN is not answered: FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.1% vs FY2025A 17.5%, gap -1.38pp, and the section 3 explanation of the earnings build is arithmetically wrong (the forecast is clean, not reported). The only qc_justification is weights.changed, and scenarios.asymmetry is an orphan with no matching flag [S15, S6].

signoff.notes: Desk sign-off, INDUSTRIALS / CONGLOMERATES, round 2. All four round-1 return points are answered on the text, and I verified each one. L1: Section 4 'What the price implies' now states the target Rp4,567 is 8.7% below the Rp5,000 price with TR -0.7%, and the implied 24.0% market discount is placed at the narrow end of the card's 20-40% range, not its midpoint - the direction of the call is now correct. L2: the signed bias audit labels the 35% discount optimistic against the ~40% peer median and conservative only against Astra's own 30% level, keeps the 25/30/35/40 sensitivity, and states the HOLD survives the 30-40 band; I re-checked the arithmetic against the sensitivity grid (30% -> Rp4,946, +6.9%; 35% -> Rp4,584, -0.7%; 40% -> Rp4,222, -7.6%; 25% -> Rp5,308, +14.1%). L3: the bridge prose is restated to the filed 30 September 2026 consolidated net debt of Rp64,925bn [S15, F100] with its derivation (finserv Rp66,700bn less ex-finserv net cash Rp1,800bn [S14, F51, F50]) and labelled display-only; I confirmed neither the SOTP (which deducts parent net debt Rp2,824bn only) nor the P/E and P/BV equity values apply it. Residual: the review-packet display line still prints Rp63,049bn from the pack balance sheet (Q9 NOTE, value-neutral); it must be repointed at F100 at the next model reopen, and it is a packet artifact, not published. L4: Section 4 now states plainly that ATN's residual net assets beyond the Rp9,509bn of directly held concession rights - working capital and cash - are carried at nil, and the claim that the 22,679 book stake captures ATN earnings is removed. Substance: SOTP Rp4,276 after the 35% discount, blend Rp4,347, target Rp4,567, TR -0.7%, HOLD; listed stakes at 6 November closes [S21-S23], every unlisted block on a sourced floor, no broker or consensus number anywhere, no unverified numeral outside background. Scenarios are mirrored on the same four shocks with the base at 45% (>= 40%), and the bear is explicitly disclosed as a discount-path value with the operating breaks quantified in the text - not a hidden understatement. The batch holds one name, so the batch-bias test does not apply. Deterministic state: check PASS, model_fresh true, engine QC blocking none, facts PASS, lint PASS. The 6,391-word length against the 500-3,500 update range is accepted once - this is a full re-underwriting after the FATAL C1, with 17 review items answered and no visible padding - but it must be trimmed to range at the next refresh; it is a standing obligation, not a resolved warning.
